title: Simple extraction methods for pesticide compound-specific isotope analysis from environmental samples
author: Gilevska, Wiegert, et al.

steps.title: Prepare pesticide stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make pesticide stock solutions at 1 g L⁻¹ in dichloromethane (DCM) or acetonitrile (ACN).

steps.title: Spike and evaporate water samples
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of the 1 g L⁻¹ stock to buffered ultrapure water (13.6 g L⁻¹ monopotassium phosphate, 4 g L⁻¹ sodium hydroxide) or to environmental water, stir until the organic solvent fully evaporates, achieving target concentrations between 0.5 µg L⁻¹ and 6 mg L⁻¹. Test water volumes of 0.01, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, and 8 L.

steps.title: Solid‑phase extract water samples
steps.instruction: Process the spiked water samples with the AutoTrace 280 SPE system (Dionex, CA, USA) following EPA Method 525.2 (simultaneous extraction of up to six samples).

steps.title: Weigh and place solid samples
steps.instruction: Place 5 g of dry soil or sediment into an amber glass centrifuge tube; for plant material, use 3 g dry weight (≈85 % water content). Keep 100 % of the water present in sediment samples.

steps.title: Spike solid samples and pre‑incubate
steps.instruction: Spike each sample with aqueous pesticide solution to obtain 0.5–50 µg g⁻¹, vortex briefly, then shake on an orbital shaker at 80 rpm for at least 30 min. Incubate the tubes in the dark at 4 °C for three days.

steps.title: First organic solvent extraction (MUSE)
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of ethyl acetate (EtOAc) **or** DCM:pentane (3:1) per gram of sample, vortex for 5 s, place in an ultrasonic bath (Branson 5510, 40 kHz) for 5 min, vortex for 1 min, then centrifuge at 2400 rpm for 20 min. Transfer the supernatant to an amber glass vial.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the solvent addition, vortex, ultrasonication, vortex, and centrifugation two additional times (total of three extractions).

steps.title: Concentrate pooled extracts
steps.instruction: Evaporate the pooled supernatants at room temperature under a gentle stream of nitrogen until only the last drop remains.

steps.title: Resuspend in acetonitrile
steps.instruction: Add acetonitrile (ACN) to bring the volume to exactly 1 mL, vortex for 5 s and ultrasonicate for 5 min to ensure complete dissolution of pesticide residues.

steps.title: Clean‑up with MgSO₄ and PSA
steps.instruction: Add 75 mg anhydrous magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) and 13 mg primary‑secondary amine (PSA) sorbent (Supelco, P/N 52738) to the 1 mL solution, vortex for 30 s, then centrifuge at 2400 rpm for 5 min. Transfer the clear supernatant to a clean amber glass vial for analysis.

steps.title: First step: aqueous CaCl₂ extraction
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of 0.01 M calcium chloride (CaCl₂) to 5 g of dry soil or sediment, vortex for 5 s, ultrasonicate for 5 min, vortex again for 1 min, then centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 10 min. Collect the 10 mL aqueous supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the CaCl₂ extraction two more times to obtain a total of 30 mL aqueous extract.

steps.title: Second step: MUSE extraction of residue
steps.instruction: Extract the remaining soil/sediment residue using the MUSE protocol described in steps 4‑9, but replace the organic solvent with methanol (MeOH) as the extraction solvent.

steps.title: Liquid‑liquid extraction of aqueous fraction
steps.instruction: To the 30 mL aqueous extract, add 3 mL dichloromethane (DCM), vortex for 5 min, ultrasonicate for 5 min, then centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 5 min. Collect the DCM layer from the bottom of the vial.

substeps.instruction: Repeat the DCM addition, vortex, ultrasonication, and centrifugation two more times (total of three DCM extractions) to obtain a combined DCM volume of approximately 9 mL.

steps.title: Finalize extract for GC‑CSIA
steps.instruction: Evaporate the combined DCM extracts to dryness, resuspend the residue in acetonitrile (ACN), vortex for 30 s, ultrasonicate for 5 min, and transfer the final solution into a gas‑chromatography vial for concentration analysis and compound‑specific isotope analysis (CSIA).
